key_insight: A two-stage evolutionary hyperparameter search can make PINN training more robust by cheaply screening candidates first and fully training only the best ones.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to improve PDE-solver accuracy under fixed compute budgets when PINNs are unstable and highly sensitive to hyperparameters.
method: Use an evolutionary algorithm to explore mixed PINN hyperparameters as a black-box outer loop.
Run short low-fidelity training epochs to quickly rank candidate configurations.
Fully train only the top candidates with standard gradient-based optimization in stage two.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on Advection, Klein-Gordon, and Helmholtz problems and consistently reduced mean error versus standard training under constrained computation.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of low-fidelity screening, so overly short truncated runs may discard configurations that would have improved with longer training.
paper_title: Evolutionary Two-Stage Hyperparameter Optimization Strategies for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
